items.title: Ray Drummond interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: Charles Mingus is a perfect example of someone who obviously was a band leader and yet he had to struggle and fight to be known.

ctx.x: Yeah. Is it hard to be a band leader?

Well there are two parts to that answer. One yes, these days it’s more difficult to get gigs primarily because most people are represented. So unless you are represented, it’s not that you’re at a disadvantage it’s just that people who are the presenters are more used to now working with people, managers, agents, than musicians. I mean more and more now the business has become more institutionalized and so it’s not that the presenters don’t want to but the presenters have gotten used to working primarily with…

because of the fact that Duke always would write these wonderful, wonderful venues for him, these wonderful pieces of music, and sure he could play it with his own group but it just didn’t have the same kind of impact for him I think. I think he just got a great feeling out of playing Duke’s music too. And so it’s like Duke made sure that you had enough money to survive so it’s kind of like why bite the hand that feeds me, that sort of thing, and that also nurtures you.
